scenario: I volunteer at a winter emergency shelter that becomes overcrowded whenever temperatures drop, and because beds are limited, the shelter prioritizes people with serious medical or physical vulnerabilities. On one especially busy night, I was helping sort intake forms while staff tried to place the last available beds. The temperature outside is chilly, so anyone who is unable to be placed with a bed will face discomfort outside. A man approached my coworker and pointed out several severe medical conditions he had listed, which would move him to the top of the priority list. Later, I overheard him telling a friend that he had lied about those conditions to nab a spot inside. There are still a handful of people waiting to have their intake forms processed. If I force the man to leave the shelter, his bed will go to someone else. If I do not do this, another person will be turned away and left to experience discomfort.
entities: I,1 coworker the man spoke to,1+ other shelter staff members placing the remaining beds,1 man who lied about severe medical conditions to get a bed,1 friend of that man,1+ other people still waiting to have their intake forms processed
outcomes: The man who lied keeps a shelter bed
The man who lied stays indoors and avoids the cold outside
Another person waiting for a bed does not get that bed
Another person remains outside in the chilly weather
I experience moral discomfort from allowing the unfair bed assignment to stand
